title: Dentons partners with Legora to roll out collaborative, advanced legal AI across Europe
author: Legora

dom.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training

st.t: Legora partnerships: Adoption needs selected workflows and training
st.an: The source supports the platform-led adoption proposition by documenting Europe-wide deployment at Dentons, positioning Legora alongside an internal tool, and anticipating continued joint development. Its efficiency and client-value claims are prospective and unquantified, reinforcing the synthesis’s distinction between rollout and demonstrated outcomes.
qs: # Dentons partners with Legora to roll out collaborative, advanced legal AI across Europe  *Legora — Legora (newsroom) (2025)*  We are excited to announce our partnership with leading global law firm Dentons, to provide its lawyers with Europe-wide access to Legora’s advanced legal AI platform.

We look forward to working closely with the Legora team to further advance the platform and our AI capabilities in line with the needs of our clients and our people.”  Max Junestrand, CEO and founder at Legora:   “Dentons has a very strong track record in utilising AI, which will serve as a crucial point for further innovation and close alignment – for both the firm’s specific growth and transformation goals.

kp.k: Dentons announces Europe-wide access to Legora
kp.d: Legora’s 2025 newsroom announcement reports a partnership to provide Dentons lawyers across Europe with its legal AI platform. The rollout is presented as enabling workflow optimisation through generative AI, advanced machine learning and natural language processing, rather than as evidence of measured operational outcomes.
qs: We are excited to announce our partnership with leading global law firm Dentons, to provide its lawyers with Europe-wide access to Legora’s advanced legal AI platform.

This partnership will allow Dentons’ lawyers across the continent to leverage Legora’s generative AI, advanced machine learning, and natural language processing capabilities to optimise legal workflows.

kp.k: AI supports document review, drafting and legal research
kp.d: Legora describes prospective lawyer-facing uses: searching and reviewing thousands of documents, assisting drafting and editing, and securely researching internal and external legal databases. These are vendor claims about supported tasks and capabilities, not reported findings from a performance study.
qs: Using Legora, Dentons’ lawyers will be able to quickly and efficiently search and review thousands of documents, use it to assist with drafting and editing documents, and securely conduct research within both internal and external legal databases.

kp.k: Internal business AI complements external legal-task tooling
kp.d: The announcement situates Legora within Dentons’ European AI strategy, distinguishing the internally developed DAISY tool, launched in May 2025 for general business purposes, from the Legora partnership for legal tasks.
qs: As part of Dentons’ AI strategy for Europe, they have been expanding their AI-enabled capabilities, launching its internally developed AI tool DAISY for general business purposes in May 2025, and now partnering with Legora to power their legal tasks.

kp.k: Dentons anticipates shifting lawyer time toward client advice
kp.d: Dentons Europe CEO Wendela Raas, quoted by Legora, predicts that faster completion of time-intensive tasks will let lawyers devote more time to client-valued legal advice. She also describes planned collaboration on platform development aligned with client and staff needs. These are customer expectations and intentions, not demonstrated time savings.
qs: Rolling out the platform across our European teams will give our lawyers a considerable head start on time-intensive tasks, and the improved speed and efficiency will allow them to spend more time delivering the quality legal advice that our clients truly value.
We look forward to working closely with the Legora team to further advance the platform and our AI capabilities in line with the needs of our clients and our people.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Legora predicts that its European rollout at Dentons will accelerate document-intensive legal workflows; Dentons Europe CEO Wendela Raas predicts that the efficiency gains will free lawyers to focus on client advice.
pts.d: Legora's newsroom announcement says its platform will enable Dentons lawyers to search and review thousands of documents quickly, assist with drafting and editing, and securely research internal and external legal databases. Raas attributes the expected change to a head start on time-intensive tasks, allowing more time for quality legal advice. Legora CEO Max Junestrand additionally presents the partnership as supporting innovation and Dentons' growth and transformation goals, without specifying measurable outcomes. The source describes assistance to lawyers, not autonomous replacement, and does not predict staffing reductions or fee changes.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The claims rest on vendor descriptions and executive expectations, with prior AI adoption offered as context rather than measured evidence of results.
pts.d: The announcement reports the partnership and Dentons' earlier launch of DAISY, an internal AI tool for general business purposes. Junestrand invokes Dentons' AI track record, and Raas supplies the anticipated efficiency-to-client-advice rationale. No pilot findings, quantified time savings, benchmarks, security assessment, client outcomes or independent evaluations are supplied. The reference to thousands of documents is a claimed capability, not a reported test result.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The 2025 announcement frames the benefits prospectively, following rollout across Dentons' European teams, without a completion date or quantified delivery horizon.
pts.d: The source places the partnership after the May 2025 launch of DAISY and describes access and workflow benefits in future-oriented terms. The anticipated benefits depend implicitly on deployment and use of Legora by Dentons lawyers. Raas also envisages continuing joint platform development aligned with client and personnel needs. The source supplies no adoption targets, performance thresholds or detailed implementation conditions.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The direct users are Dentons lawyers across Europe; clients are expected to benefit indirectly from lawyers spending more time on valued advice.
pts.d: The announcement concerns a global law firm's European operations and a legal-technology vendor supplying its platform. Lawyers are expected to gain assistance with research, document review and drafting. Raas identifies clients as beneficiaries of the resulting reallocation of lawyer time, while Junestrand links the partnership to firm-level innovation, growth and transformation. No specific practice areas, seniority groups, client segments or public access-to-justice effects are identified.
